sentences.text: This document specifies GPIO hardware IP functionality.
This module conforms to the Comportable guideline for peripheral device functionality See that document for integration overview within the broader top level system.
32 GPIO ports
Configurable interrupt per GPIO for detecting rising edge, falling edge, or active low/high input
Two ways to update GPIO output: direct-write and masked (thread-safe) update
Second, per-pin register view to assign individual GPIOs to different software components, e.g., CHERIoT compartments
The GPIO block allows software to communicate through general purpose I/O pins in a flexible manner.
Each of 32 independent bits can be written as peripheral outputs in two modes.
Each of the 32 bits can be read by software as peripheral inputs.
How these peripheral inputs and outputs are connected to the chip IO is not within the scope of this document.
See the Comportability Specification for peripheral IO options at the top chip level.
In the output direction, this module provides direct 32b access to each GPIO value using direct write.
This mode allows software to control all GPIO bits simultaneously.
Alternately, this module provides masked writes to half of the bits at a time, allowing software to affect the output value of a subset of the bits without requiring a read-modify-write.
In this mode the user provides a mask of which of the 16 bits are to be modified, along with their new value.
The details of this mode are given in the Programmers Guide below.
In the input direction, software can read the contents of any of the GPIO peripheral inputs.
In addition, software can request the detection of an interrupt event for any of the 32 bits in a configurable manner.
The choices are positive edge, negative edge or level detection events.
A noise filter is available through configuration for any of the 32 GPIO inputs.
This requires the input to be stable for 16 cycles of the module clock before the input register reflects the change and interrupt generation is evaluated.
Note that if the filter is enabled and the pin is set to output then there will be a corresponding delay in a change in output value being reflected in the input register.
See the Design Details section for more details on the features.
The block diagram above shows the DATA_OUT and DATA_OE registers managed by hardware outside of the auto-generated register file.
For reference, it also shows the assumed connections to pads in the top level netlist.
The GPIO module maintains one 32-bit output register DATA_OUT with two ways to write to it.
Direct write access uses DIRECT_OUT, and masked access uses MASKED_OUT_UPPER and MASKED_OUT_LOWER.
Direct access provides full write and read access for all 32 bits in one register.

For masked access the bits to modify are given as a mask in the upper 16 bits of the MASKED_OUT_UPPER and MASKED_OUT_LOWER register write, while the data to write is provided in the lower 16 bits of the register write.
The hardware updates DATA_OUT with the mask so that the modification is done without software requiring a Read-Modify-Write.
Reads of masked registers return the lower/upper 16 bits of the DATA_OUT contents.
Zeros are returned in the upper 16 bits (mask field).
To read what is on the pins, software should read the DATA_IN register.
(See GPIO Input section below).
The same concept is duplicated for the output enable register DATA_OE.
Direct access uses DIRECT_OE, and masked access is available using MASKED_OE_UPPER and MASKED_OE_LOWER.
The output enable is sent to the pad control block to determine if the pad should drive the DATA_OUT value to the associated pin or not.

A typical use pattern is for initialization and suspend/resume code to use the full access registers to set the output enables and current output values, then switch to masked access for both DATA_OUT and DATA_OE.

For GPIO outputs that are not used (either not wired to a pin output or not selected for pin multiplexing), the output values are disconnected and have no effect on the GPIO input, regardless of output enable values.
In addition to the 32-bit registers, which group the GPIOs by function, the GPIO module provides a second register view that groups them by pin.
This view allows assigning individual GPIOs to different software components, for example to CHERIoT compartments, by granting each component access to only the registers of its GPIOs.
Both views alias the same state, and a write to a per-pin register only affects the GPIO it belongs to.
The per-pin view consists of two separate, aligned address ranges, so access to the data of a GPIO can be granted without access to its configuration:
PER_PIN_IO holds one register per GPIO with bit i of DATA_OUT and of DATA_IN.

The configuration range holds two registers per GPIO, which directly follow one another: PER_PIN_OE_0 with bit 0 of DATA_OE, PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_0 with bit 0 of the interrupt control and input filter registers, then PER_PIN_OE_1, PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_1, and so on.
A register write must cover all bytes of the register that hold a field, so access cannot be granted to only some fields of a register.
The output enable and the interrupt configuration of a GPIO are therefore in separate registers, so access to one can be granted without the other.
The interrupt registers INTR_STATE, INTR_ENABLE and INTR_TEST have no per-pin view.

Like the interrupt controller, they are expected to be managed by a trusted software component, for example a trusted CHERIoT compartment, which handles the GPIO interrupts on behalf of the components owning the GPIOs.
The DATA_IN register returns the contents as seen on the peripheral input, typically from the pads connected to those inputs.
In the presence of a pin-multiplexing unit, GPIO peripheral inputs that are not connected to a chip input will be tied to a constant zero input.
The GPIO module provides optional independent noise filter control for each of the 32 input signals.
Each input can be independently enabled with the CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER (one bit per input).
This 16-cycle filter is applied to both the DATA_IN register and the interrupt detection logic.
The timing for DATA_IN is still not instantaneous if CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER is false as there is still both top-level routing delay and input CDC synchronizer delay involved.
The top-level routing delay depends on the physical layout of the chip.

The input synchronizer adds two flops between the chip input and the DATA_IN register, though the added delay may vary by up to one GPIO clock cycle depending on when cycle each external input transition arrives relative to the GPIO clock.
The contents of DATA_IN are always readable and reflect the value seen at the chip input pad regardless of the output enable setting from DATA_OE.

If the output enable is true (and the GPIO is connected to a chip-level pad), the value read from DATA_IN includes the effect of the peripheral's driven output and will only differ from DATA_OUT if the output driver is unable to switch the pin or during the delay imposed by the input synchronizer and noise filter (if enabled).
The GPIO controller provides an optional feature to sample GPIO input values as hardware configuration straps.
After each reset, on the first cycle when the strap_en_i signal is asserted, the GPIO detects its transition from low to high.
One clock cycle later, it samples the GPIO input values and stores them in the HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN register.
The strap_en_i signal transition from low to high is expected only once after the reset process.
Sampling occurs exclusively at this time, and any subsequent changes to the GPIO input configuration will not be captured.
This mechanism samples all 32 bits of the GPIO input data, regardless of the GPIO output enable status, providing a reliable snapshot of the input values for firmware access.
The GPIO module provides 32 interrupt signals to the main processor.
Each interrupt can be independently enabled, tested, and configured.

Following the standard interrupt guidelines in the Comportability Specification, the 32 bits of the INTR_ENABLE register determines whether the associated inputs are configured to detect interrupt events.
If enabled via the various INTR_CTRL_EN registers, their current state can be read in the INTR_STATE register.
Clearing is done by writing a 1 into the associated INTR_STATE bit field.
For configuration, there are 4 types of interrupts available per bit, controlled with four control registers.
INTR_CTRL_EN_RISING configures the associated input for rising-edge detection.
Similarly, INTR_CTRL_EN_FALLING detects falling edge inputs.
INTR_CTRL_EN_LVLHIGH and INTR_CTRL_EN_LVLLOW allow the input to be level sensitive interrupts.
In theory an input can be configured to detect both a rising and falling edge, but there is no hardware assistance to indicate which edge caused the output interrupt.
Note #1: The interrupt can only be triggered by GPIO input.
Note #2: All inputs are sent through optional noise filtering before being sent into interrupt detection.
Note #3: All interrupts to the processor are level interrupts as per the Comportability Specification guidelines.
The GPIO module, if configured, converts an edge detection into a level interrupt to the processor core.
Initialization of the GPIO module includes the setting up of the interrupt configuration for each GPIO input, as well as the configuration of the required noise filtering.
These do not provide masked access since they are not expected to be done frequently.
This section below shows the interaction between the direct access and mask access for data output and data enable.
This section below gives an example of how interrupt clearing works, assuming some events have occurred as shown in comments.
Use the per-pin register view when individual GPIOs belong to different software components, for example CHERIoT compartments.
Grant each component access to only the per-pin registers of its GPIOs, and keep using the 32-bit registers in software that manages all GPIOs, for example during initialization.
The per-pin registers of GPIO i are:
PER_PIN_IO_i at offset 0x100 + 4 * i: data_out in bit 0 and the read-only data_in in bit 8.
PER_PIN_OE_i at offset 0x200 + 8 * i: oe in bit 0.
PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_i at offset 0x204 + 8 * i: the rising-edge, falling-edge, level-high and level-low interrupt enables in bits 0 to 3, and the input filter enable in bit 4.
PER_PIN_IO_i has fields in bytes 0 and 1, so a write to it must cover both bytes, i.e., be at least 16 bits wide.
A byte write returns an error and has no effect, so a capability for PER_PIN_IO_i must cover at least these two bytes.
PER_PIN_OE_i and PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_i also accept byte writes.
The interrupt registers INTR_STATE, INTR_ENABLE and INTR_TEST have no per-pin view.
They are expected to be managed by a trusted component, which handles the GPIO interrupts on behalf of the components owning the GPIOs.

sections.title: ot_gpio_nnc: integration of the OpenTitan gpio for verification

sentences.text: Written for NNC Pipeline.

This document describes the verification top ot_gpio_nnc: the OpenTitan gpio (specified by the OpenTitan parts of this document, above) plus a thin wrapper that flattens its struct ports and closes two protocols.
The behaviour of gpio itself is specified only by the OpenTitan documents; this document adds the port mapping, the configurations and what the wrapper does.
Normative references:
the OpenTitan parts of this document (above): the GPIO block, its registers, interrupts, straps and alert.
standards/opentitan_tlul_bus_specification.md: the TL-UL bus, including the bus integrity scheme.
standards/opentitan_comportability.md: interrupt and alert conventions of OpenTitan peripherals.
standards/opentitan_register_tool.md: register access types and bus error responses of generated register blocks.
standards/opentitan_alert_handler_theory_of_operation.md: the differential alert handshake and the alert receiver.
[INT-CFG-001] The design under verification has 32 GPIOs, as stated in the Features section.
[INT-CFG-002] RACL (register access control) is disabled: every register access is permitted, and no access is rejected for an access-control reason.
[INT-CFG-003] The alert sender of gpio and the alert receiver of the wrapper both use the synchronous clocking scheme (no synchronizer flops on the differential pairs).
Ping requests are never issued.
[INT-CFG-004] Two design parameters of gpio are parameters of ot_gpio_nnc and are passed through unchanged:
Parameter: GpioAsyncOn; Default: 1; Legal values: 0 or 1; Description: "Instantiates 2-flop synchronizers on all GPIO inputs if set to 1." (gpio parameter list)

Parameter: GpioAsHwStrapsEn; Default: 1; Legal values: 0 or 1; Description: "Enable HW straps sampling logic for GPIO inputs at initial cold boot" (gpio parameter list); the behaviour of HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN for each value is given in its register description
[INT-CFG-005] The verification shall be run in every combination of the two parameters that the run set selects; the default combination (1, 1) is the configuration of the Earl Grey top level.
[INT-CLK-001] clk_i is the only clock.
All TL-UL and strap inputs are sampled and all outputs change at its rising edge, except for the effect of rst_ni.
[INT-CLK-002] With GpioAsyncOn = 1, i_gpio may change at any time relative to clk_i (an input from a pad).
With GpioAsyncOn = 0 there is no synchronizer, and the test bench shall change i_gpio only synchronously to clk_i, like the other inputs.
[INT-RST-001] rst_ni is the active-low reset, asserted asynchronously and released synchronously to clk_i (the reset strategy of the comportability specification).
While rst_ni is 0, every register holds its reset value as given in the register tables of the gpio specification.

[INT-TL-001] The i_a_*, o_a_ready, o_d_* (except o_d_intg_err) and i_d_ready ports are the fields of the same name of the TL-UL device interface tl of gpio, with the meaning given by the TL-UL bus specification.
[INT-TL-002] a_user.rsvd is 0. a_user.instr_type is MuBi4True when i_a_instr is 1 and MuBi4False when it is 0.
[INT-TL-003] The test bench acts as the TL-UL host.
It shall follow the host rules of the TL-UL bus specification (for example, the A-channel signals stay stable while a_valid is 1 and a_ready is 0).

Requests that the TL-UL specification lists as error cases (unsupported opcode, bad size or mask, misaligned address) are legal stimulus: the device answers them with d_error = 1 as the specifications require.

[INT-INTG-001] The wrapper computes a_user.cmd_intg and a_user.data_intg of every request with OpenTitan's integrity generator for TL-UL hosts (the section Bus Integrity Scheme of the TL-UL bus specification is not written yet; the code is not part of this specification).
A request with i_a_intg_flip = 0 therefore always carries correct integrity, and the test bench does not compute integrity itself.
[INT-INTG-002] When i_a_intg_flip is 1, bit 0 of a_user.cmd_intg is inverted.
The request then has a command integrity error: a fatal TL-UL bus integrity fault in the sense of the gpio Security Alerts table, which triggers the fatal_fault alert (section 5).
These documents do not specify the D-channel response to such a request.

[INT-INTG-003] The wrapper checks d_user.rsp_intg of every D-channel beat against the response fields with OpenTitan's response integrity checker for TL-UL hosts. o_d_intg_err is 1 in a cycle where o_d_valid is 1 and this check fails, and 0 otherwise.
A correct device never makes it 1.
[INT-ALERT-001] gpio has one alert, fatal_fault, sent through an alert sender.

The wrapper connects it to an alert receiver as described in the alert handler theory of operation (Differential Alert Signaling). o_alert is the alert_o output of that receiver: it is 1 for one clock cycle for each alert handshake that the receiver detects.
[INT-ALERT-002] o_alert_integ_fail is the integ_fail_o output of the receiver.
A correct sender never makes it 1.
[INT-ALERT-003] A fatal alert is repeated until reset (comportability specification, Alerts per Module), so after a bus integrity fault o_alert pulses repeatedly until rst_ni is asserted.
A write of 1 to ALERT_TEST.fatal_fault triggers one alert event, as the register description says.
[INT-IO-001] i_gpio, o_gpio and o_gpio_en are the peripheral pins cio_gpio_i, cio_gpio_o and cio_gpio_en_o of gpio: bit i belongs to GPIO[i]. o_gpio is DATA_OUT and o_gpio_en is DATA_OE.
[INT-IO-002] There is no pad model and no pin multiplexer in ot_gpio_nnc: i_gpio is driven only by the test bench and does not depend on o_gpio or o_gpio_en.

The Programmer's Guide examples assume pads with weak pull-ups connected to the outputs; a test that follows such an example models the pad itself (for example by driving i_gpio[i] = o_gpio[i] where o_gpio_en[i] = 1 and 1 elsewhere).

[INT-INTR-001] o_intr_gpio[i] is the interrupt output intr_gpio_o[i] of gpio, an event-type interrupt as defined in the comportability specification, with bit i of the registers INTR_ENABLE, INTR_STATE and INTR_TEST.

[INT-STRAP-001] i_strap_en is the input strap_en_i of gpio, and o_straps_valid and o_straps_data are the fields valid and data of its output sampled_straps_o (Inter-Module Signals table, GPIO Inputs as HW Straps).

[INT-VER-001] The verification shall cover, through the ports above and in each configuration of the run set: reset values of every register; the access type of every register field as given in the register tables; direct and masked writes of DATA_OUT and DATA_OE and their reads; the per-pin register view; DATA_IN with and without the input filter; interrupt detection on rising edge, falling edge, high level and low level, with INTR_STATE, INTR_ENABLE and INTR_TEST; strap sampling with HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN_VALID and HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN; bus error responses (unmapped addresses, sub-word writes, instruction fetches, integrity errors) and the fatal_fault alert.
[INT-VER-002] The per-pin registers of 32 GPIOs behave alike.
The verification may check every GPIO for the 32-bit registers and a selection of GPIOs for the per-pin registers, provided that the selection includes GPIO[0], GPIO[15], GPIO[16] and GPIO[31].
The gaps that nnc spec-lint found in this specification (work/spec_lint.md, GAP-001..019) are answered here, from the documents only.
Where the documents are silent or disagree, the verification checks only what every reading has in common, or a bound instead of an exact cycle.
These decisions were taken on the project owner's delegation by an AI assistant, not by a hardware designer; the G4 reviewer is asked to confirm them.

ID: D-001; Subject: Masked writes of DATA_OE (GAP-001); Decision: The register descriptions bind, and the Theory of Operation says the masked-write concept "is duplicated for the output enable register": a write to MASKED_OE_LOWER (MASKED_OE_UPPER) sets DATA_OE[i] to data bit i where mask bit i is 1 and leaves every other bit of DATA_OE unchanged, exactly as for DATA_OUT. The DATA_OE values in the Programmer's Guide example are not used as expected values.

ID: D-002; Subject: Read of MASKED_OE_* bits 31:16 (GAP-002); Decision: Bits 15:0 of a read of MASKED_OUT_* and MASKED_OE_* are the corresponding half of DATA_OUT / DATA_OE. Bits 31:16 of a read of MASKED_OUT_* are 0. For MASKED_OE_* the text says 0 and the field table says rw: bits 31:16 of a read are not checked.

ID: D-003; Subject: Reset values (GAP-003); Decision: The "Reset default" line of each register binds where the field table says "x": DIRECT_OUT, DIRECT_OE, MASKED_*, INTR_CTRL_EN_*, CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER, PER_PIN_OE_i, PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_i and PER_PIN_IO_i.data_out read 0 after reset, and o_gpio and o_gpio_en are 0 while rst_ni = 0 and until written. DATA_IN and PER_PIN_IO_i.data_in are not checked while rst_ni = 0 and in the first 20 cycles after release.

ID: D-004; Subject: INTR_ENABLE and detection (GAP-004); Decision: The gpio text makes INTR_ENABLE a condition for detection; the comportability specification makes it only mask the output. Checked, as both readings agree: with INTR_ENABLE[i] = 1 a configured event sets INTR_STATE[i]; with INTR_ENABLE[i] = 0, o_intr_gpio[i] stays 0. INTR_STATE[i] after an event that occurs while INTR_ENABLE[i] = 0 is not checked, and neither is o_intr_gpio[i] in the 4 cycles after INTR_ENABLE[i] is set to 1 when such an event may have been latched.

ID: D-005; Subject: W1C while a level condition holds (GAP-005); Decision: If the level condition still holds after a write of 1 to INTR_STATE[i], INTR_STATE[i] reads 1 and o_intr_gpio[i] (with INTR_ENABLE[i] = 1) is 1 again within 4 cycles after the write response; a dip in between is not checked.

ID: D-006; Subject: Event in the same cycle as a W1C (GAP-006); Decision: Not checked: tests do not create an edge on GPIO[i] within 8 cycles of a write of 1 to INTR_STATE[i], or do not check INTR_STATE[i] after it.

ID: D-007; Subject: Input filter threshold and switching (GAP-007); Decision: With CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER[i] = 1: a new value of i_gpio[i] held for at most 12 cycles never appears in DATA_IN[i] and creates no interrupt event; a new value held for at least 24 cycles appears in DATA_IN[i] no later than 24 cycles after the change. The exact threshold is not checked. After a write that changes CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER[i], DATA_IN[i] and interrupt events of GPIO[i] are not checked for 24 cycles; tests keep i_gpio[i] constant in that window.

ID: D-008; Subject: Strap sampling (GAP-008); Decision: With GpioAsHwStrapsEn = 1, tests keep i_strap_en = 0 while rst_ni = 0 and for at least 4 cycles after release, then raise it once and keep i_gpio constant from 24 cycles before to 8 cycles after that rising edge. Within 4 cycles after the edge, HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN_VALID reads 1, o_straps_valid = 1, and HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN and o_straps_data equal that i_gpio value. Before the edge both valid indications are 0. Later changes of i_gpio or i_strap_en change neither until reset; after a reset ("After each reset", Theory of Operation) the sequence can happen again. A level already high at reset release is not used.

ID: D-009; Subject: Straps disabled (GAP-009); Decision: With GpioAsHwStrapsEn = 0, HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN reads 0 at all times (register description). HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN_VALID, o_straps_valid and o_straps_data are not checked.

ID: D-010; Subject: ALERT_TEST (GAP-010); Decision: Tests that trigger an alert write 0x8000_0001 (regwen kept at 1); the combined write 0x0000_0001 is not used. A write with bit 31 = 0 sets regwen to 0 until reset; afterwards a write of 0x8000_0001 completes with d_error = 0, triggers no alert, and regwen still reads 0. One write of 1 to fatal_fault, with no other alert cause and no other such write within 32 cycles, gives exactly one o_alert pulse, no later than 16 cycles after the write response. After reset ALERT_TEST reads 0x8000_0000.

ID: D-011; Subject: Instruction fetches (GAP-011); Decision: Not stated for registers in these documents. A request with i_a_instr = 1 is not checked for d_error; a write with i_a_instr = 1 is not used.

ID: D-012; Subject: Address decoding (GAP-012); Decision: Following the register tool (excess address bits are stripped), the registers 0x000..0x2fc use the offsets 0x000..0x3FF. A request to an unmapped offset in 0x000..0x3FF returns d_error = 1 and changes no register. Requests at 0x400 and above are not used.

ID: D-013; Subject: Sub-word and partial writes (GAP-013); Decision: Per the register tool and the Per-Pin Register View text: full-word writes with mask 1111 succeed. An aligned byte write (a_size 0 at offset 0 of the register, mask 0001) to a register with fields above bit 7 (INTR_*, DIRECT_*, MASKED_*, INTR_CTRL_EN_*, CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER, PER_PIN_IO_i) returns d_error = 1 and changes nothing; such a byte write to PER_PIN_OE_i or PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_i completes with d_error = 0 and has the effect of the write. Other sub-word cases, including a_size 2 with a partial mask, are not checked. Reads of any size return the full register.

ID: D-014; Subject: Outstanding requests and back-pressure (GAP-016); Decision: TL-UL allows several outstanding requests and does not guarantee order. The test bench matches responses by d_source, uses a distinct a_source per outstanding request, and does not assume o_a_ready = 1.

ID: D-015; Subject: Fields of a response (GAP-018); Decision: Checked: d_error, d_source (echo of a_source), d_size (echo of a_size), d_opcode (AccessAckData for Get, AccessAck for PutFullData and PutPartialData). d_data is checked only for a Get without error. For an undefined opcode only d_error = 1 is checked. d_param and d_sink are not checked.

ID: D-016; Subject: Reset (GAP-017); Decision: The test bench keeps i_a_valid = 0 while rst_ni = 0 and in the first cycle after release. While rst_ni = 0, o_d_valid, o_alert, o_alert_integ_fail, o_intr_gpio, o_gpio and o_gpio_en shall be 0; o_a_ready, o_straps_valid and o_straps_data are not checked. A response pending at reset is discarded. The rule that outputs change only at rising clock edges is not applied in cycles where rst_ni is 0 or falls.

ID: D-017; Subject: Integrity outputs and integrity errors (GAP-014); Decision: o_d_intg_err and o_alert_integ_fail shall be 0 in every cycle with rst_ni = 1. After a request with i_a_intg_flip = 1 is accepted, o_alert shall pulse no later than 16 cycles later and then at least once in every 32 cycles until rst_ni is asserted. The D-channel response to that request, its effect on registers and the behaviour of later requests are not checked; the test bench does not wait more than 32 cycles for that response, and the test resets the design afterwards.

ID: D-018; Subject: Latencies (GAP-015); Decision: With the filter off, a change of i_gpio[i] held for at least 8 cycles appears in DATA_IN[i] no later than 4 cycles after the first rising edge after the change (both values of GpioAsyncOn). A configured event sets INTR_STATE[i] no later than 4 cycles after it appears in DATA_IN[i]. o_intr_gpio[i] equals INTR_STATE[i] AND INTR_ENABLE[i] except in the 2 cycles after either changes. o_gpio and o_gpio_en equal DATA_OUT and DATA_OE no later than 2 cycles after the response of the write that changed them. Lower bounds are not checked.

ID: D-019; Subject: Writes to read-only registers, reads of write-only fields (GAP-018); Decision: A write to a ro register or field (DATA_IN, HW_STRAPS_*, PER_PIN_IO_i.data_in) leaves it unchanged; its d_error is not checked. A wo field (INTR_TEST, MASKED_OUT_* mask, ALERT_TEST.fatal_fault) has no read path and reads 0 (register tool, Type WO). Reserved bits read 0 and writes to them have no effect.

ID: D-020; Subject: Programmer's Guide comments (GAP-019); Decision: The register names and descriptions decide: INTR_CTRL_EN_LVLLOW and INTR_CTRL_EN_LVLHIGH enable level detection, not edge detection. The comments of the examples are not used as expected behaviour.

ID: D-021; Subject: Pins and the pad model; Decision: DATA_IN reflects i_gpio only (INT-IO-002): with o_gpio_en[i] = 1 the test bench may drive i_gpio[i] to any value, and DATA_IN[i] follows i_gpio[i], not o_gpio[i].

ID: D-022; Subject: Out of scope; Decision: User-bit default values, requests with a non-zero a_param, and the bit layout of a_user/d_user (the wrapper produces them) are not checked; tests drive i_a_param = 0.

The register descriptions bind, and the Theory of Operation says the masked-write concept "is duplicated for the output enable register": a write to MASKED_OE_LOWER (MASKED_OE_UPPER) sets DATA_OE[i] to data bit i where mask bit i is 1 and leaves every other bit of DATA_OE unchanged, exactly as for DATA_OUT. The DATA_OE values in the Programmer's Guide example are not used as expected values.

Bits 15:0 of a read of MASKED_OUT_* and MASKED_OE_* are the corresponding half of DATA_OUT / DATA_OE. Bits 31:16 of a read of MASKED_OUT_* are 0. For MASKED_OE_* the text says 0 and the field table says rw: bits 31:16 of a read are not checked.

The "Reset default" line of each register binds where the field table says "x": DIRECT_OUT, DIRECT_OE, MASKED_*, INTR_CTRL_EN_*, CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER, PER_PIN_OE_i, PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_i and PER_PIN_IO_i.data_out read 0 after reset, and o_gpio and o_gpio_en are 0 while rst_ni = 0 and until written. DATA_IN and PER_PIN_IO_i.data_in are not checked while rst_ni = 0 and in the first 20 cycles after release.

The gpio text makes INTR_ENABLE a condition for detection; the comportability specification makes it only mask the output. Checked, as both readings agree: with INTR_ENABLE[i] = 1 a configured event sets INTR_STATE[i]; with INTR_ENABLE[i] = 0, o_intr_gpio[i] stays 0. If the level condition still holds after a write of 1 to INTR_STATE[i], INTR_STATE[i] reads 1 and o_intr_gpio[i] (with INTR_ENABLE[i] = 1) is 1 again within 4 cycles after the write response; a dip in between is not checked.

Not checked: tests do not create an edge on GPIO[i] within 8 cycles of a write of 1 to INTR_STATE[i], or do not check INTR_STATE[i] after it.

With CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER[i] = 1: a new value of i_gpio[i] held for at most 12 cycles never appears in DATA_IN[i] and creates no interrupt event; a new value held for at least 24 cycles appears in DATA_IN[i] no later than 24 cycles after the change. The exact threshold is not checked. After a write that changes CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER[i], DATA_IN[i] and interrupt events of GPIO[i] are not checked for 24 cycles; tests keep i_gpio[i] constant in that window.

With GpioAsHwStrapsEn = 1, tests keep i_strap_en = 0 while rst_ni = 0 and for at least 4 cycles after release, then raise it once and keep i_gpio constant from 24 cycles before to 8 cycles after that rising edge. Within 4 cycles after the edge, HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN_VALID reads 1, o_straps_valid = 1, and HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN and o_straps_data equal that i_gpio value. Before the edge both valid indications are 0. Later changes of i_gpio or i_strap_en change neither until reset; after a reset ("After each reset", Theory of Operation) the sequence can happen again. A level already high at reset release is not used.
With GpioAsHwStrapsEn = 0, HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN reads 0 at all times (register description). HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN_VALID, o_straps_valid and o_straps_data are not checked.

Tests that trigger an alert write 0x8000_0001 (regwen kept at 1); the combined write 0x0000_0001 is not used.
